items.title: Using the stack-frame tests as design-enforcement tool.
items.box:
Using the stack-frame tests as design-enforcement tool.

WHAT EXISTS (paths under spirit/test/)
- tools/wirePaths.js records, during the suites it drives, every call stack inside our own code that reaches a bottom, and ranks the paths. A stack sees where code arrives, not what it resembles, so it finds a second route to the same place even when no name or text is shared.
- Its bottoms: wire (the network), fs-write, crypto, child-process, and two components, presenceNode and postQueue.
- oneDoorStacks.js (goal/G19.14) is the enforcing suite: one test per bottom that names a door. It runs that row's suites and fails on any stack with a production frame (spirit/run/) and no frame in the door. Stacks with no production frame are a suite unit-testing the component and are not counted. A run that never reaches the component fails.
- Two doors are enforced today: nobody but peerPost reaches presenceNode, and nobody but peerPost reaches postQueue.
- oneDoorStacks.js is part of run all: runAll.js and deskVerify's full run both take every suite in spirit/test.

HOW IT ENFORCES A DESIGN
- A design rule of the form "only this door may reach that component" becomes one row: the door, the component, and the suites that drive it.
- The wire, fs-write, crypto and child-process bottoms are measured but have no door yet; each ruling such as "only X writes to disk" costs one row.

ITS LIMIT
- It sees only the paths the driven suites walk: a row is as good as its suites, and a path no suite exercises stays invisible.

ITEMS
- goal/G22.3: the gg plugin, a goal-governance plugin desk mounts from its plugin folder.

chat.text: thoughts?

2. It is part of run all: runAll.js lists it, and so does deskVerify's full run, since both take every suite in spirit/test. It is not stand-alone.

Its limit: it sees only the paths the driven suites walk, so a row is as good as its suites; an empty run already fails.

now we create a new item for another stack-path we want to control, inside peerPost

suggestions?

Of peerPost's components, two are worth a row next:
1. sseClient, the stream to a relay: only peerPost and presenceNode (itself a peerPost component) use it today, so the row locks in a state that is already clean. The cheapest.
2. seal, the one sealing implementation: on the node side only peerPost uses it; hub, relay and relayServer use it on the relay side, so that row needs one door per side. The most valuable: a second sealing path is how associated data gets dropped.
I'd take sseClient first; say which and I propose the item.
can you name one you know would fail?

Yes: "nobody but peerPost talks to a relay". The desk's offboard.js fetches the relay's key straight from the relay over plain fetch (process/js/desk/offboard.js line 78), so a wire row with peerPost as its door fails on it, as long as a driven suite runs offboard.
A softer one: relayKeys, the relay table, is read outside peerPost by answerRelay, ownerBadge and server.js; that fails too, but reading a table may be allowed by design.
I'd take the offboard one: it is a real second road to a relay.
make THAT one an item.
Added: goal/G22.2, "Nobody but peerPost talks to a relay"; its box holds the rule and what will make it fail.

Ok. Now we have arrived at this point:

the red for 22.2 has verified that the entry for no direct call to relays is as row in the stack-frame check. great.

what i want now, is the first desk-plugin: it a 'gg' goal-governance plugin, where the plugin sets the parameters (Gate-Frame / Target Frame)and generates the equivalent of a 22.2 type item.

the "create-goal" inputs in the default panel of desk, will offer a dropdown for goal type: default [generic], and this first plugin will handle new stack frame items, and govern the goal, by inserting itself ahead for desks event/input handler. the plugin itself will ensure that the goal always stays open, that 22.1 is always open, etc... if the done-button is ever seen or not.

make sense?

It makes sense: a goal type picked at create-goal, generic by default; a stack-frame goal is governed by the gg plugin, which turns a gate frame and a target frame into a 22.2-type item and refuses Done and Close on the goal and on its rerun item, ahead of desk's own handling.
What would make it work without an agent each time: the doors become data (one file listing gate, target and suites) that wirePaths and stackFrameTestItems read, so the plugin adds a door by writing a row of data, not by editing test code.
The one thing it cannot know by itself is which suites drive a door; that is measured, so either a generated item carries a measuring step for an agent, or the row starts on the whole harness.
And the plugin hook ahead of desk's handler is a new extension point in desk.js, so its shape is a design item of its own.
Shall the first item be that hook, or the doors-as-data file?

a gg-plugin is simply a goal-governance plugin, it implies that for this type of goal, it is the first to handle events. those are the mechanical controls it can implement.

it has a companion dialog, where the gate and endpoint functions can be entered. for that goal, (or a bubble in the goal-dialog itself, i'd prefer a dialog, where the items of this goal, 

it's sort of like a pluggable version of goal/G0 that is also a special goal, always "open" (it's actually closed)

Yes. A gg plugin owns its goal type: it sees every event for that goal first, and its mechanical controls (no Done, no Close, the rerun item kept open) live there instead of in desk.js.
That is what goal/G0 already is, hard-wired: desk.js special-cases desk/G0.0 in about ten places (closed from the start, no buttons, no verify, never regresses, never brought back). A gg plugin is the same thing made pluggable, so the group chat could later become a plugin too.
The companion dialog takes the gate and endpoint for a new door and makes the 22.2-type item.

items.title: Nobody but peerPost talks to a relay
items.box:
Nobody but peerPost talks to a relay.

DECIDED (Andy, 2026-10-13)
- The purpose of this item is to add one row to the stack-frame test (oneDoorStacks.js, through tools/wirePaths.js): every request our production code sends to a relay must have peerPost on its stack. That is all it does.
- Its red goes into another suite, stackFrameTestItems.js in spirit/test, which asserts that this row exists in the stack-frame test; it is red until the row is added and green after.
- The row is committed failing on purpose: oneDoorStacks and goal/G22.1 are meant to fail, so that a pattern can be developed that guides the fixes for this kind of failure. The fixes come in later items, not in this one.

FOUND (b29bf3ac, 2026-10-13; paths under spirit/run/)
- Relay traffic is told apart by path: every request under /api/relay/, which a relay answers and a node never does, so a process asking its own node is not counted even when a lab relay also listens on loopback.
- The probe also watches global fetch, which never passes through http.request.
- The row is driven by agentOnboard.js (the only suite that runs offboard) and serverSurface.js.
- The row finds 7 paths to a relay without peerPost: process/js/desk/offboard.js line 78 (fetch of the relay key); and through js/relayRequest.js, from js/hub.js (key at 300 and 2651, claim at 1084), js/ownerBadge.js 369 (directly and via hub 2784), and js/answerRelay.js 35 (key).

items.title: gg plugin: goal governance by a mounted plugin
items.box:
gg plugin: goal governance by a mounted plugin.

DECIDED (Andy, 2026-10-13)
- A gg plugin is a goal-governance plugin: for its type of goal it is the first to handle every desk event, and the mechanical controls it implements live there, not in desk.js.
- No goal-type choice at create-goal: desk scans its plugin folder and mounts every plugin it finds; the first plugin governs stack-frame goals.
- The stack-frame plugin sets the parameters (gate frame and target frame) and generates the equivalent of a goal/G22.2 item from them.
- It governs its goal: the goal always stays open, and its rerun item (as goal/G22.1) always stays open, whether a Done button is ever seen or not.
- It has a companion dialog where the gate and endpoint functions are entered.
- It is a pluggable version of goal/G0: a special goal that is always open while actually closed.
- On its first mount the plugin gets its own private goal with a fixed key, and from then on that goal and the plugin live hand in hand; the goal has its chat, box and everything else for free, and in the list of goals it shows a button in the label column that opens the plugin's private UI.

THIS RENDITION (Andy, 2026-10-13) does only:
- Mount every plugin in desk's plugin folder, organized with the same pattern as shell apps and processes.
- The stackFrameChecks plugin, governing in full in this item: its goal and its rerun item always stay open, and its dialog takes a gate and an endpoint and makes the goal/G22.2-type item.
- In the main list, a button replacing the label of each plugin's private goal, which opens the plugin's private UI.
- When this item is done, a goal "Maintain this plugin" follows.
- The plugin folder: each plugin's server half at spirit/run/process/js/desk/plugins/js/<name>/<name>.js with its .json beside it, its private UI at spirit/run/shell/desk/plugins/<name>/.
